goal: Produce conditional theorems about the single-seed Rule 30 center column, not more finite exclusions. Each obligation must name a lemma, the prize implication it buys, and the cheapest thing that could refute it.
settled: s*(n) for base-2 MSD DFAOs is exact at s*(48)=12, s*(52)=12, s*(56)=13, s*(64)=15. Finite exclusions only.
Every left diagonal is eventually periodic (proved). The measured settling law settle(d) ~ 1.3389*d is empirical, not an all-horizon theorem.
The period-16 conjecture is refuted by a measured period-32 diagonal. Unboundedness and period(d) ~ 2*log2(d) remain observational conjectures, not settled theorems.
GF(2) linear complexity L(n)=n/2 is maximal; no LFSR shortcut.
Uniform Bernoulli is invariant, so Prize 2 is trivial for random ICs and its difficulty is entirely in the single seed.
Algebraic complexity over F_2(x) is maximal on the center column to N=1024, inside the 7-seed random band at 4 of 4 lengths. Finite prefix; not a proof of non-automaticity.

obligations.lemma: For every finite positive-half seed r>=0, the unique forced negative completion e_j(r) for c_t=t mod 2 satisfies W_N(r)=sum_{j<=N} e_j(r)>=alpha(r)N-C(r) for all N>=1, for some alpha(r)>0 and finite C(r).
obligations.implication: A stronger sufficient lemma: infinite negative weight excludes a finite alternating trace; advancing a nonzero finite row to a zero phase excludes eventual period two. The weaker W_N(r)->infinity assertion is equivalent to the original finite-configuration period-two question, not a reduction.
obligations.refutation: An exact physical prefix can refute a specified numerical pair alpha,C. Finite absence of violations cannot prove their existence for every r; a sparse infinite completion could disprove positive density while leaving period-two exclusion true.

mechanism_check.ensemble-not-orbit: The universal finite-configuration theorem would include the single seed; no ensemble average or free boundary is substituted for the actual orbit.
mechanism_check.partial-map-assumed-total: Ordered support obligations must follow the same physical H^k(r), including every OR reset and unresolved continuation; no total finite-state map is assumed.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: The finite SAT curve proves only bounded minima. The proposed inequality quantifies over every N and remains entirely unproved, not an extrapolated grade.

obligations.progress: 2026-10-14: Condrey period-one argument audited in-session (Proof candidate); its monotone latch becomes s_next=(1-s)(1-u)(1-v) under alternation. Right seeds1 and7 have the same leading one but force different left bits at depth9. Existing transfer/renewal work credited; density bound entirely unproved. docs/theory/period2_attempt.md.

obligations.lemma: The generating function f(x) = sum c_n x^n of the single-seed center column is transcendental over F_2(x).
obligations.implication: Prize 3 only. Correction 2026-09-18: this is NOT a Prize 1 route. Over a finite field a power series is rational iff its coefficients are eventually periodic, so Prize 1 is exactly irrationality - the D=1 case. Algebraicity (D>=2) is strictly stronger than Prize 1 needs, so a transcendence proof is a harder target than the prize it was filed under. It removes automatic-sequence shortcuts from Prize 3 in base 2, and nothing more.
obligations.refutation: experiments/algebraic_relation.py finds a bounded-degree relation that extrapolates onto held-out coefficients. The instrument is calibrated: it recovers the textbook Thue-Morse relation (D=2, E=3, C*=12) and that budget plateaus in N, which is the signature a genuine shortcut would show.

mechanism_check.forced-outcome: The search is a kernel over F_2 with C=(D+1)(E+1) unknowns against N constraints, so a fit is forced whenever C exceeds N. The instrument therefore reports the minimal budget C*(N) as a curve against a random null and a Thue-Morse positive control, and additionally requires any fit to predict coefficients it never saw, which is not forced at any budget.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: A negative at budget C and length N is recorded as a bounded finding. The asymptotic content is carried only by the shape of the C*(N) curve, plateau versus growth, and never by any single point.

obligations.progress: 2026-09-18: C*(N) is now measured rather than absent. Center is MAXIMAL, inside the 7-seed null band at 4 of 4 lengths to N=1024, against an 85x-separated Thue-Morse control, cross-checked by an independent numpy rank. The lemma is unrefuted and sharper: the finite evidence now says maximal algebraic complexity, not merely no small relation. Next: push past N=1024, which needs a packed-word or GPU rank because the elimination is O(N^3/64), and widen the null band.

obligations.lemma: Any description of the unsettled core of the light cone that supports O(polylog t) random access to the center column requires Omega(t) bits.
obligations.implication: This is Prize 3 restricted to the only region that matters: the theory gate proves the settled wedge is O(t)-describable and disjoint from the center column, so a lower bound on the core is the whole of Prize 3 for cone-based methods.
obligations.refutation: Exhibit a sub-linear description of the core that reproduces center bits, or show the core's block entropy falls below the matched random control at any scale. The gate already measures pre-settle block-entropy rate >= 0.9975 against 0.99961 for the control.

mechanism_check.disjoint-from-prize-object: The measured settling law places the centre in the unsettled core at tested horizons. Its empirical coefficient must not be used as an all-horizon theorem.
mechanism_check.ensemble-not-orbit: The quantity is measured on the single seed light cone and is never averaged or perturbed over initial conditions, so it is a property of the prize orbit rather than of the rule.

obligations.lemma: Determine whether the exact single-seed centre forcing sum sum_{s<t} [z^0] L^{t-1-s} Q_s admits an efficient compressed representation or random access, or establish a lower bound in a specified computation model; L=z^-1+1+z and Q_s=sum_i a_s(i)a_s(i+1)z^i.
obligations.implication: The exact Rule 150 Duhamel identity locates the failure of homogeneous additive propagation, not a complexity barrier. Rule 30 differs from Rule 90 by a linear centre term as well as the quadratic product. Any Prize 3 implication needs a seed-specific compression theorem or a lower bound in a defined model.
obligations.refutation: For a proposed lower-bound mechanism, exhibit a representation or shortcut within its specified model. A variable-change barrier must define its allowed transformations first.

mechanism_check.algebra-already-gives-it: The additive baseline and exact Duhamel identity are settled algebraically; the remaining obligation concerns a seed-specific forcing compression or a lower bound in a defined model.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: Finite identity checks support the symbolic derivation only. No runtime barrier or forcing non-compressibility follows from those checks, and a model-specific proof is still required.

obligations.progress: 2026-10-14: symbolic diagnosis completed: the all-time Duhamel identity and superposition defect are proved and checked on all 32 five-cell seeds for every t<=64. Rule 90 and zero filters pass. No hardness bound established. docs/theory/nonlinear_obstruction.md; experiments/nonlinear_obstruction_check.py.

obligations.lemma: The left-diagonal period satisfies period(d) = Theta(log d), and the constant is exactly 2 in the measured regime.
obligations.implication: NONE. Demoted 2026-09-18: this is independent cone theory with no prize bridge. The automaticity-to-bounded-period route that would have used it is closed (see theory/README.md section 4), and the cone is in any case provably disjoint from the centre column because settle(d) ~ 1.34d > d. Worth proving as a structural theorem about the light cone; not prize progress, and not to be given prize priority.
obligations.refutation: Find a diagonal whose period departs from the 2*log2(d) law. The doubling criterion is already a Theorem - the branch fires exactly at a consecutive-word collision w_{d-2} = w_{d-1} with odd parity - so the open lemma is that infinitely many such events occur. Note period(d) ~ 2*log2(d) is a Robust observation, NOT a Theorem: what is proved is only that d=87867 has period 32, i.e. periods are not bounded by 16. Unboundedness itself is unproved.

mechanism_check.partial-map-assumed-total: The earlier cycle and reachability routes died because the pair of pattern words is not a complete state and the orbit escapes at every zero word. This obligation targets the rate at which the doubling branch fires, and never assumes a total map or looks for a cycle.
mechanism_check.disjoint-from-prize-object: Diagonal periodicity does not touch the center column directly, so the implication is stated as structure about the cone rather than as a Prize 1 proof, and it is scoped accordingly.

obligations.lemma: No DFAO with at most 20 states in base 2 MSD generates the first 128 bits of the center column.
obligations.implication: Would add one more point to the s*(n) curve. Note the 14-state n=64 refutation already cost 353s and a 2.26GB proof, and difficulty rose about 10x per state, so 20 states at n=128 is far beyond reach.

mechanism_check.forced-outcome: Not vacuous by counting: log2|M| for 20 states in base 2 is about 192.9 against n=128, so the negative would discriminate. The objection to this obligation is cost and value, not vacuity.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: This buys one more point on a curve that is already exact at four lengths, and says nothing about bit 129, so its implication is thin even if the search succeeds.
